To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the level of knowledge re-use increases as the amount of feedback in peer conversations increases and (b) the level of re-use increases when the majority of feedback is positive rather than negative.

1) displaying sentiment-driven feedback toward peers’ work positively influenced the level knowledge reuse in Wikipedia and 2) displaying mainly positive feedback toward peers’ knowledge work corresponded to a higher level of knowledge reuse compared to displaying mainly negative feedback.

1) Wikipedia editors communicate their feedback to each other in the form of positive and negative sentiments, and 2) displaying positive sentiments positively influences the level of knowledge re-use in Wikipedia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How do Wikipedia editors communicate their feedback toward other’s contributions?
how peer feedback influences the level of knowledge sharing in online communities.
how peer feedback influences the level of knowledge reusability in a wiki-based online community.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this research are in line with previous research on knowledge reuse in Wikipedia, but also extend the knowledge base in this area.
the impact of sentiment-driven feedback on knowledge reuse depends on the type of feedback.
sentiment-driven feedback positively influences the level of knowledge re-use in Wikipedia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that displaying sentiment driven feedback can have a positive impact on knowledge reuse in online communities.
the way peers communicate their feedback toward other peers’ work has a significant impact on the level of knowledge re-use in Wikipedia.
the impact of feedback in online social production is not just about the content of the feedback.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way peers are motivated to contribute knowledge to a wiki-based knowledge reuse system is important for the system’s success.
the design of wiki systems should be based on the assumption that displaying sentiment-driven peer feedback will positively influence the level of knowledge production.
the way in which peers provide each other with feedback is important for knowledge reuse.
